text.p: Alexandre Lamfalussy, head of the European Monetary Institute, said the so-called "stability pact" for countries in the future euro currency zone was a useful and important initiative, afternoon daily Le Monde said on Thursday.
"The pact is a useful and very important initiative," he told the newspaper in an interview.
The pact, proposed by Germany to ensure budgetary discipline for countries taking part in a single euro currency, has caused disagreements between Bonn and other European governments.

"It will have a dissuasive effect," Lamfalussy said of the pact. "But, even if this pact is respected, we can conceive of sudden changes in the financing needs of a large country with unnacceptable consequences for others," he said.

"To avoid this, there must be ex ante coordination of policies. Finance ministers must agree among themselves, talk among themselves. It would be important for this to imagine an appropriate mechanism."
Lamfalussy said that while any outside control of the European Central Bank's policy would be in complete contradiction to the Maastricht treaty, a dialogue would not.
"It would be in the interests of the ECB as well as the governments," he said of this dialogue.
